newsitem.title: USA: S.F. Fed's Parry says US economy in good position.
newsitem.headline: S.F. Fed's Parry says US economy in good position.

text.p: The U.S. economy is in a good position amid robust growth and well-behaved inflation, Robert Parry, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, said Monday.

"Looking at where we are now, I think it's fair to say that our efforts to strike the right balance have worked well for the country's economy," Parry said in prepared remarks to a conference sponsored by the bank and the Tucson Chamber of Commerce.
Parry was describing the Fed's efforts to achieve a balance between short-run measures of economic performance and long-run efforts to promote sustainable growth.
He said the economy was "currently in a good position" amid a "long recovery, robust growth (and) well-behaved inflation."
He added, "(The) economy (is) now slowing to a moderate -- and I hope, sustainable -- pace, with no clear signs of an end to the recovery."

Discussing the long-run goals of monetary policy, the San Francisco Fed chief said: "Keeping inflation low is the best way a central bank can promote maximum sustainable growth and employment, which are the keys to the nation's economic health."

Speaking broadly about how the Fed conducts monetary policy, Parry emphasized that the central bank takes into account economic activity in regions across the country but it cannot not direct policy toward any specific region or state.
Ultimately, he said, "the object of monetary policy has to be the economic health of the nation as a whole."
